clue.text: Friend has a supply of food stimulating the taste-buds

parts.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written
a table is the food provided at meals, as in 'she keeps a good table'

explanation.surface: A friend arrives with a store of delicious food.
explanation.definitionFit: Something palatable is pleasant to eat, so it appeals to the palate and tongue.

clue.text: At great speed — so the past is dissipated

indicators.note: something dissipated is scattered and dispersed, so these letters are broken up and regrouped

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Time rushes by so quickly that the past melts away.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an old adverb meaning with all possible haste, originally from urgent letters sent by post riders.

clue.text: A city — does this imply LA?

parts.note: surface reading: a question about whether some place is the abbreviation for Los Angeles
setter's reading: break the city's name into a single letter, a verb of possession and an article, and the sentence it forms describes those two capitals side by side

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether some city name is shorthand for Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tibetan capital, read as three words, describes the two letters L and A sitting together.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital of Tibet, an ancient Himalayan city and seat of the Dalai Lama.

clue.text: Heavy work without lubricants achieved with difficulty

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: one word stands around the other

parts.note: a tome is a large weighty book
oils lubricate machinery

explanation.surface: Hard physical labour done with no oil to ease the machinery is a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy work' looks like labour, but it is a big book; 'without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilsome means laborious, describing a task that demands strenuous effort and is hard going.

clue.text: Refuse stamps for fines

parts.note: bran is the husk left over from milling grain, a waste product
dies are tools that stamp designs onto coins or metal

explanation.surface: Rubbish and postage stamps are handed in to pay off penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fines' looks like penalties, but a fine is also a French brandy, as in fine champagne cognac.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine is a term for good-quality French brandy, so plural fines are brandies.

clue.text: No more wine — that's the limit

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
tent is a deep red Spanish wine once used for communion

explanation.surface: The wine has run out, and that is the final straw.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is an old name for a dark red wine from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The extent of something is how far it reaches, its boundary or scope.

clue.text: Poetic man who went to pot?

definitions.text: Poetic man who went to pot?

parts.words: Poetic man who went to pot?
parts.note: surface reading: a poet who let himself go to ruin

parts.words: Poetic man who went to pot?
parts.note: setter's reading: a man's name that is also a herb, famous in Keats's poem where a pot of this herb is planted over a head

explanation.surface: A poet who fell into decline and dissipation.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats's poem 'Isabella, or the Pot of Basil' has the heroine bury her lover's head in a herb pot; the herb is also a man's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a male first name and a culinary herb grown in pots, made famous in a Keats poem.

clue.text: Song that's naughty with everyone joining in

indicators.note: something joining in enters the middle of the group, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a naughty child is bad
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A rude singalong where the whole crowd joins the chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song or poem, often sentimental, sung in short stanzas.

clue.text: The man's an illustrator — see him at the port

parts.note: a typical man's first name
Gustave Doré, the French engraver who illustrated Dante and the Bible

explanation.surface: An artist is pointed out down at the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Doré is the famous nineteenth-century French book illustrator; the accent is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a docker who loads and unloads ships, so he works at a harbour.

clue.text: Fortune given to you and me — it may induce indolence

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune or fate
us is you and me together

explanation.surface: A windfall handed to the two of us may make us lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Odyssey the lotus-eaters ate a fruit that left them dreamy and idle, forgetting home.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's lotus fruit made those who ate it lazy and forgetful, hence 'lotus-eater' for an idler.

clue.text: Strength shown by parts of flower not often seen

definitions.text: parts of flower not often seen
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a rare plural of stamen, the pollen-bearing organ

explanation.surface: Power displayed by rarely glimpsed flower parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual plural of stamen is stamens; the Latin-style plural is rare, hence 'not often seen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means endurance and is also an uncommon plural of a flower's pollen-bearing organ.

clue.text: A couple of students in exam head and shoulders above the rest?

definitions.text: head and shoulders above the rest?

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the word for the paper being sat

parts.note: a test is an exam
taken as written
L for learner, twice

explanation.surface: Two students sitting an exam come out far ahead of everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner sign, so a student is L. The definition is literal: the tallest stands head and shoulders above others.
explanation.definitionFit: Being head and shoulders above the rest literally means greatest in height, the superlative of tall.

clue.text: Those who lead one side? They don't always turn up!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: leaders, chiefs of departments or schools

definitions.text: one side? They don't always turn up!
definitions.meaning: second meaning: one face of a tossed coin, which lands upward only about half the time

explanation.surface: Team leaders who are unreliable about showing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' sounds like arriving at a meeting, but it is a coin landing face upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaders of schools or departments are called this, and it is also the obverse face of a coin.

clue.text: Boiler suits range used for cooking

indicators.note: cooking means mixing and changing ingredients, so these letters are stirred into new order

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Overalls are worn in a kitchen with a stove in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a cooker, tying in with 'cooking', but it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are hard-wearing overalls, much like the one-piece garments worn by workers tending boilers.

clue.text: Instrumentalist = stranger on the street

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
rum means odd, so rummer means odder

explanation.surface: A busker is a stranger playing on the pavement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun for an unknown person, but it is the comparative adjective, odder; 'on' puts it after the street in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strummer plays a guitar or similar stringed instrument by sweeping the strings, so is a musician.

clue.text: River journey groan desperately having fallen in

indicators.note: something that has fallen in has dropped inside, so these letters sit within the other word

parts.note: a ride is a journey

indicators.note: acting desperately means flailing wildly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A passenger on a river trip moans miserably after falling overboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande is the large North American river forming much of the US border with Mexico.

clue.text: Take care of mother in life-threatening condition

parts.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Look after your mum when she is gravely ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take care of' looks like a single verb, but the useful part is the address abbreviation for 'care of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coma is a state of deep prolonged unconsciousness, which can be fatal.

clue.text: The wind comes over the isle harshly

parts.note: Auster is the Roman name for the south wind
the Isle of Ely, a former fenland island in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A cruel gale sweeps across an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Auster is the classical south wind; Ely is the Cambridgeshire city still called the Isle of Ely. In a down answer, 'comes over' puts the wind on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To act austerely is to act severely and sternly, without softness or comfort.

clue.text: Larva carries a germ unfortunately in fruit

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so the larva wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a bot is the larva of the botfly

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so these letters are set amiss

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A maggot inside a piece of fruit is infected with something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The bot is the larva of a botfly, a parasite of horses and sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: The bergamot is a citrus fruit whose rind oil flavours Earl Grey tea.

clue.text: Dangerous gas got rid of a politician

parts.note: to fire someone is to get rid of them from a job
taken as written
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A noxious gas finished off a politician, or the hot air was got rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is methane in coal mines, which forms explosive mixtures with air.

clue.text: Wild rose as the symbol of love

indicators.note: wild means untamed and disorderly, so these letters run loose into another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild rose stands for love.
explanation.walkthrough: The rose is itself a famous love symbol, which makes it tempting as a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of desire, whose figure represents romantic passion.

clue.text: Study Buddhist sect found among island inhabitants

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for working

indicators.note: something found among others sits in their midst, so the sect goes inside

parts.note: Is is an abbreviation for island
Zen is a Japanese school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: Students of a Buddhist sect turn up among the people of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Denizens are residents or occupants of a particular place.

clue.text: Indian moving speedily reins in horse's head

indicators.note: to rein in a horse is to hold it back, so one letter is held inside

parts.note: apace means quickly

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of horse

explanation.surface: A Native American on a galloping horse pulls the reins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a Native American people of the south-western United States.

clue.text: The pictures s obtained from spies including revolutionary workers

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the spies surround the workers

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the word for workers is read backwards

parts.note: men as in workmen, a workforce

explanation.surface: Photographs sourced from secret agents who are hiding left-wing labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pictures' is British for the cinema, as in going to the pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage 'the pictures' means a cinema, the place where films are shown.

clue.text: Big thrashing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tall and sturdy, burly
second meaning: a beating with a leather strap

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it seems a heavy beating; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a robust, powerfully built person, while the noun is a whipping with a belt.

clue.text: Very good salesman, American, on the up

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An excellent American salesman whose career is rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal praise meaning excellent or first-rate.

clue.text: A bird but not a birdie

definitions.text: A bird but not a birdie

parts.words: A bird but not a birdie
parts.note: surface reading: a full-grown bird rather than a little one

parts.words: A bird but not a birdie
parts.note: setter's reading: a bird of prey whose name is also a golf score two under par, one better than a birdie

explanation.surface: A grown bird, not a tiny one.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf a birdie is one stroke under par for a hole; the next score down shares its name with a large raptor.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey, and in golf the term means two strokes under par.

clue.text: Gee — relative's become bony and emaciated!

parts.note: gee is how the letter G is spelt out
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: An exclamation of shock at how thin a family member has become.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gee' looks like a cry of surprise but is the spelt-out name of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaunt describes someone haggard and very thin, with the bones showing through.

clue.text: Face pain in a grand manner

parts.note: pan is slang for the face
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Bear suffering with dignity and flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' looks like a verb meaning confront, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence and style, a dashing flair.

clue.text: One's for one in play

parts.note: surface reading: some sort of team swap or trade in a game
setter's reading: the title of a Shakespeare comedy names the same word twice joined by 'for'

explanation.surface: A like-for-like exchange during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's 'Measure for Measure' has the same noun either side of 'for'; the clue replaces both with 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word appears twice in Shakespeare's play title, once on each side of 'for'.

clue.text: Magistrate appearing in the Case of the Wicked Lady

parts.note: re means in the case of, concerning
Eve, who tempted Adam in Eden

explanation.surface: A judge presides over a sensational trial about a scandalous woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Wicked Lady' sounds like a film title, but it is Eve, the first sinner in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a chief officer or local magistrate in medieval English towns and districts.

clue.text: Opposed to the State — your old aversion

parts.note: anti means against
PA is Pennsylvania, a US state
thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: Your former hostility to government.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipathy is a deep-seated dislike or hostility felt toward something.
